name: RC22 H1 (old): Loss Rebalancing (IS=0.005, VS=1.0)
result: 166a: 5/9 best, 4/9 final. S4 perfect (1.000), S8 median_bias PASS. But S2 still FAIL. IS reduction was the primary driver.

name: RC22 H1 (v2): Factorized Decoder with Split Conditioning
theory: Post-attention noise injection via L@eps prevents rank compression. Split conditioning via FiLM.
result: 167a: 5/9 (S3 regression). L died from 4 confounded issues (WD 27x, FiLM bug, oversized head, CLN competition). Codex-verified x2.

name: RC22 H1 (v3): Clean Isolation Test (167b)
theory: Remove all 4 confounds from 167a. Binary diagnostic: can L@eps work at all?
result: 167b: 6/9 in 20 epochs. L alive (norm 0.12, growing). Factor directions align with GT (PC1: 0.93, PC2: 0.82). Per-cell spread matches GT (r=0.979). BUT: mean reversion collapsed to 12% GT because CLN was frozen. Not end-to-end viable (CLN freeze is unprincipled). Codex: solved diagnostic, not practical frontier (CI 0.811 vs baseline 0.813).

name: RC22 H1 (v4): End-to-End Factorized — CLN Active (167d)
theory: 167b proved L can work when confounds removed. The key question: can L survive with CLN active and trainable? Keep only the standard/publishable fixes: (2) wd=0 for load_head+FiLM, (3) FiLM (1+gamma)*h+beta, (4) simple Linear load_head. Drop fix (1) CLN freeze — let CLN train normally. Train from scratch. If L survives → factorization is end-to-end viable. If L dies → CLN competition IS the fundamental blocker, not WD/FiLM/head-size.
target: L_norm stable (not dying). L_eff_rank >2.5. MR slope near baseline (-0.22). S3 PASS. Total >= 6/9.
kill_condition: L_norm declines like 167a. base/load grad ratio returns >3. L_eff_rank stays ~2.
if_fails: Factorization is dead as publication path under end-to-end constraint. Pivot to loss-level research (H5 K reduction, H6 stop-gradient routing).
result: 167d: 5/9 (S3 worst-cell FAIL). L survived e2e (L_norm 0.07-0.14 stable). BUT doesn't beat baseline. Gradient asymmetry (not competition): CLN dominates 15-24x at edge cells. Sampled MR=67% GT. Factorization solves trainability, not the frontier.

name: RC22 H5: K Reduction (K=4, end-to-end centering probe)
theory: Low K increases centering/spread gradient ratio within CRPS. K=16 centering/spread=1.07. K=4 should give ~1.5x. SOTA uses K=2-4 (FGN, AIFS-CRPS). End-to-end, philosophy-consistent, directly targets S2 centering which is the real frontier blocker. Confirmed by 6 Codex reviews.
target: S2 centering improves. Sampled MR slope closer to GT. Individual scenarios more authentic.
kill_condition: Spread collapses (std < 50% baseline). Or S4 kurtosis destroyed. Or S9 correlation breaks.
note: Highest priority. Directly targets the REAL blocker (centering, baseline ~56% GT). Does not depend on factorization. Centering protocol: measure BOTH deterministic + sampled mean slopes.

name: RC22 H2: K Reduction (K=8, B=32) — original
theory: SOTA uses K=2-4. Our K=16 has centering/spread ratio 1.07. K=8 gives 1.14.
note: Superseded by H5 (K=4 is more aggressive and Codex-recommended). Keep for reference.

name: RC22 H3: Encoder Contrastive Loss
theory: Encoder condition 98% shared. InfoNCE pushes regimes apart.
note: Issue was not encoder discrimination (167a investigation proved). Low priority.

name: RC22 H4: Structure Loss on Factor Loadings
theory: Add explicit rank incentive: -logdet(L^T L + εI). afCRPS only rewards ||l_c|| (row norm), not orthogonality.
note: Only relevant if factorization survives (H1v4 passes). Otherwise moot.

name: RC22 H6: Loss-Routing — Stop-Gradient on Spread Through Base Path
theory: Change optimization geometry so base_head gets centering gradient but spread gradient routes only through L@eps. Keeps CRPS end-to-end. Not an auxiliary loss — a gradient routing modification. Prevents the base path from being corrupted by spread pressure. Codex-suggested in review #4.
target: Base_head learns centering (MR slope near GT). L@eps handles spread/diversity. Both active end-to-end.
kill_condition: Stop-gradient kills training stability or breaks convergence.
note: Only if H1v4 fails AND H5 insufficient. This is the loss-level research direction. Requires careful design — which gradient components to stop where.

name: RC22 H1 (v3b): Warm-Start Factorized (167c) — DIAGNOSTIC ONLY
theory: Warm-start from baseline to test upper bound: can factor path + baseline centering coexist? Copy output_proj -> base_head, add load_head with wd=0, two-phase training.
target: L alive + MR preserved at baseline level (50% GT).
note: NOT end-to-end. NOT publishable as mainline method. Only for mechanistic understanding if 167d fails. Codex review #4: 'lower information gain per GPU hour than 167d'.
